parsed.explanation: The division itself has no current bathroom ban or trans-specific criminal offence; the 2016 birth-certificate bathroom rule was repealed and the 2025 bill remains pending, so facility exposure is an open legislative risk rather than a settled local prohibition. But the parent regime binds every visitor: passport/visa sex-marker restrictions, entry screening that can refuse or scrutinise discrepant documents, possible prolonged detention, and federal single-sex facility exclusion create a universal, traveller-facing exposure with no demonstrated working remedy. State recourse is thin: the hate-crime statute omits gender identity, statewide public-accommodation protection is absent, and local ordinances cover only parts of the population. National custody practice is documented as harmful. The 3.0-per-100k trans-women figure is an acknowledged undercount floor, so I treat violence as undocumented rather than assessed. This is Elevated Risk, below profiles with pervasive service denial or statewide facility bans, but above reduced-risk jurisdictions with functioning visitor-facing remedies.
